applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: diaphoresis or autonomic symptoms can occur
a dangerous cause requires prompt exclusion
edges.plausible_error: The learner overweights chest pain and danger while ignoring the territorial ischemic ECG change and dynamic troponin pattern.
edges.neighboring_choice: Pulmonary embolism as the cause of acute chest symptoms.
edges.decisive_discriminant: PE becomes competitive with sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, VTE risk, or a probability-linked PE work-up; the stem instead supplies a regional ischemic ECG change and dynamic troponin rise without those PE features.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if PE probability features make PE equal or more likely.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: a life-threatening vascular cause is possible
edges.plausible_error: The learner treats any severe chest pain in a hypertensive patient as dissection despite absent high-risk aortic features.
edges.neighboring_choice: Acute aortic syndrome as the cause of chest pain.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Dissection is supported by abrupt maximal-onset chest/back pain, pulse or blood-pressure differences, or malperfusion; the stem explicitly lacks those features and instead has a territorial ischemic pattern.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if abrupt maximal pain, pulse deficit, neurologic deficit, or aortic regurgitation makes AAS genuinely competitive.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: pain may follow a recent viral illness in some cases
edges.plausible_error: The learner sees chest pain plus an ST change and recalls pericarditis without checking pain quality or territorial versus widespread ECG distribution.
edges.neighboring_choice: Acute pericarditis as an inflammatory chest-pain syndrome.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Pericarditis is characteristically sharp, pleuritic, positional, and associated with widespread ST elevation or PR depression; the stem has pressure-like exertional pain and regional ischemic ST depression.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the pain is pleuritic/positional or the ECG is diffuse rather than territorial.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: symptoms can be described as burning or pressure
edges.plausible_error: The learner anchors on a recent meal or retrosternal burning and prematurely labels reflux.
edges.neighboring_choice: GERD as a noncardiac cause of retrosternal symptoms.
edges.decisive_discriminant: GERD is favoured by heartburn/regurgitation and is established only after adequate cardiac evaluation for unexplained chest pain; regional ischemic ECG change with a dynamic troponin rise cannot be dismissed as reflux.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the stem lacks objective ischemia or supplies dominant typical reflux features after cardiac causes are addressed.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: both pathways can involve biomarkers and urgent imaging
edges.plausible_error: The learner substitutes a generic dangerous-chest-pain work-up for probability-directed PE testing.
edges.neighboring_choice: D-dimer followed by CTPA as a PE diagnostic pathway.
edges.decisive_discriminant: D-dimer/CTPA is probability-driven for suspected PE; absence of dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, VTE risk, or PE-likely assessment leaves serial ECG and hs-cTn as the scenario-bound ACS investigation.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the case has moderate/high PE probability or a positive probability-linked D-dimer.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: initial cardiac tests may be nondiagnostic
edges.plausible_error: The learner equates severity with aortic catastrophe and orders CTA without aortic risk features.
edges.neighboring_choice: Immediate CT angiography of the aorta.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Aortic CTA is indicated when acute aortic syndrome is suspected from abrupt maximal pain or malperfusion features; those are absent, while persistent ischemic suspicion after early nondiagnostic tests calls for serial ECG and hs-cTn.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the history or examination raises genuine acute aortic syndrome suspicion.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: echocardiography can be relevant in both cardiac disorders
edges.plausible_error: The learner orders inflammatory markers and echocardiography after recalling pericarditis from any chest pain.
edges.neighboring_choice: Pericarditis-directed inflammatory and effusion assessment.
edges.decisive_discriminant: The case lacks pleuritic/positional pain and widespread ST/PR changes; its early nondiagnostic ACS tests require serial ECG and hs-cTn rather than a pericarditis-first pathway.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if pericarditic pain, diffuse ECG changes, rub, or effusion evidence is present.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: normal early cardiac tests can tempt premature closure
edges.plausible_error: The learner interprets one normal early troponin and ECG as adequate exclusion of ACS and pivots to reflux testing.
edges.neighboring_choice: Upper endoscopy or reflux monitoring for GERD.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Objective GERD testing for chest pain follows adequate cardiac evaluation; one early nondiagnostic ECG and hs-cTn do not complete that evaluation when ACS suspicion persists.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if an adequate cardiac evaluation is complete and typical reflux/alarm features make GI testing the active decision.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: primary PCI is generally preferred when timely
edges.plausible_error: The learner knows primary PCI is preferred but ignores the scenario's first-medical-contact-to-device delay above 120 minutes.
edges.neighboring_choice: Transfer for primary PCI without giving fibrinolysis.
edges.decisive_discriminant: At a non-PCI centre with an expected device time beyond 120 minutes, no contraindication, early presentation, and low bleeding risk, Canadian guidance supports fibrinolysis rather than accepting the excessive untreated delay.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if primary PCI can be achieved within 120 minutes or fibrinolysis is contraindicated.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: clinical and ECG reperfusion can be assessed locally
rescue PCI is needed after failed lysis
edges.plausible_error: The learner remembers rescue PCI but omits routine pharmacoinvasive transfer after apparently successful lysis.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis and transfer only if reperfusion fails.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Canadian pharmacoinvasive guidance requires routine rapid PCI-centre transfer after fibrinolysis and angiography within 24 hours even when reperfusion appears successful.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if transfer is genuinely unavailable and the item explicitly tests contingency planning rather than the recommended pathway.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: cardiac troponin is central to myocardial infarction classification
serial testing is appropriate for nondiagnostic suspected ACS
chest pain can have nonischemic causes
edges.plausible_error: The learner overgeneralizes the serial-troponin rule from uncertain NSTE-ACS to an ECG-diagnostic STEMI.
edges.neighboring_choice: Wait for serial high-sensitivity troponin before selecting reperfusion.
edges.decisive_discriminant: The stem establishes diagnostic STEMI; current ACS guidance states that reperfusion must not be delayed pending biomarkers.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the ECG is nondiagnostic and the case truly requires serial testing before classification.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
edges.plausible_error: The learner responds to severe pain and hypertension with an aortic pathway despite absent acute-aortic discriminants and a diagnostic territorial STEMI.
edges.neighboring_choice: Begin anti-impulse therapy and obtain urgent aortic CTA.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Aortic anti-impulse therapy and CTA require suspected acute aortic syndrome; the case lacks abrupt maximal-onset pain, pulse/BP asymmetry, and malperfusion and instead has diagnostic STEMI requiring immediate reperfusion.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if high-risk aortic features make dissection a genuine competing emergency.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select cautious intravenous crystalloid preload support for hypotension due to right ventricular infarction rather than giving preload-reducing treatment.
shared_features: inferior STEMI with ongoing ischemic discomfort
edges.plausible_error: The learner treats ischemic pain reflexively with nitrate without recognizing preload-dependent RV physiology.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give sublingual nitrate despite hypotension and right-ventricular preload dependence
edges.decisive_discriminant: Hypotension, elevated JVP, clear lungs, and right-sided ST elevation indicate RV preload dependence; nitrate reduces preload and is specifically avoided, whereas cautious IV fluid with reassessment addresses the physiology.
excluded_contexts: Exclude hemodynamically stable ACS without suspected RV infarction.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select cautious intravenous crystalloid preload support for hypotension due to right ventricular infarction rather than giving preload-reducing treatment.
edges.plausible_error: The learner equates elevated JVP with left-sided volume overload and gives a loop diuretic despite clear lungs.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give intravenous loop diuresis despite clear lungs
edges.decisive_discriminant: Clear lungs plus elevated JVP and V4R elevation point to RV infarction rather than pulmonary congestion; diuresis reduces preload, while cautious IV fluid optimization is the indicated initial maneuver.
excluded_contexts: Exclude pulmonary edema or demonstrated fluid overload where diuresis may be indicated.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select cautious intravenous crystalloid preload support for hypotension due to right ventricular infarction rather than giving preload-reducing treatment.
shared_features: beta blockade can be appropriate after stabilization
edges.plausible_error: The learner applies routine early post-MI beta blockade without checking for hypotension and low output.
edges.neighboring_choice: Escalate beta blockade during hypotension
edges.decisive_discriminant: A low-output or shock-risk state is a contraindication to early beta-blocker initiation or escalation; first optimize RV preload and stabilize hemodynamics, then reassess beta blockade.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a hemodynamically stable post-MI patient without low output, acute HF, bradycardia, or conduction block.

applicable_learner_decisions: Prioritize emergency coronary revascularization while concurrently initiating shock support when acute myocardial infarction causes cardiogenic shock.
shared_features: vasopressors may be needed for perfusion support
edges.plausible_error: The learner mistakes temporary blood-pressure support for treatment of the infarct-related cause.
edges.neighboring_choice: Use vasoactive support without urgent revascularization
edges.decisive_discriminant: Vasoactive support may run concurrently, but AMI cardiogenic shock carries a class I indication for emergency culprit-vessel revascularization irrespective of symptom-onset time.
excluded_contexts: Exclude shock from a noncoronary cause or a mechanical defect requiring a different definitive intervention.

applicable_learner_decisions: Prioritize emergency coronary revascularization while concurrently initiating shock support when acute myocardial infarction causes cardiogenic shock.
edges.plausible_error: The learner waits for complete shock resolution before addressing the culprit coronary lesion.
edges.neighboring_choice: Defer angiography until shock has fully resolved
edges.decisive_discriminant: Treatment delay worsens survival in AMI shock; emergency angiography and culprit-vessel revascularization proceed with concurrent stabilization rather than after full shock resolution.
excluded_contexts: Exclude situations in which goals of care or a prohibitive noncardiac condition preclude invasive treatment.

applicable_learner_decisions: Prioritize emergency coronary revascularization while concurrently initiating shock support when acute myocardial infarction causes cardiogenic shock.
shared_features: a cautious fluid assessment can be part of initial shock care
edges.plausible_error: The learner treats persistent hypoperfusion as generic volume depletion despite established AMI cardiogenic shock.
edges.neighboring_choice: Use intravenous fluid resuscitation alone
edges.decisive_discriminant: Persistent hypotension with end-organ hypoperfusion from AMI requires causal emergency revascularization; fluid alone neither opens the culprit artery nor constitutes definitive shock treatment.
excluded_contexts: Exclude isolated hypovolemia without evidence of AMI-related pump failure.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select aspirin plus guideline-concordant parenteral anticoagulation as initial antithrombotic treatment for confirmed NSTE-ACS when no bleeding contraindication is present.
edges.plausible_error: The learner generalizes the STEMI lytic pathway to every myocardial infarction.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis for NSTE-ACS
edges.decisive_discriminant: Fibrinolysis is an eligible-STEMI reperfusion pathway; confirmed NSTE-ACS instead receives antithrombotic therapy and risk-stratified invasive evaluation.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a true STEMI or posterior occlusion pattern that belongs on an immediate reperfusion pathway.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select aspirin plus guideline-concordant parenteral anticoagulation as initial antithrombotic treatment for confirmed NSTE-ACS when no bleeding contraindication is present.
edges.plausible_error: The learner selects one correct component and overlooks upstream anticoagulation for confirmed type 1 NSTE-ACS.
edges.neighboring_choice: Use aspirin alone
edges.decisive_discriminant: Aspirin loading is required but does not replace guideline-concordant parenteral anticoagulation initiated at NSTE-ACS diagnosis when no contraindication is present.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a patient with a true contraindication to anticoagulation or a diagnostic reclassification away from type 1 ACS.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select aspirin plus guideline-concordant parenteral anticoagulation as initial antithrombotic treatment for confirmed NSTE-ACS when no bleeding contraindication is present.
shared_features: parenteral anticoagulation is required in NSTE-ACS
edges.plausible_error: The learner selects anticoagulation but omits the initial antiplatelet component.
edges.neighboring_choice: Use parenteral anticoagulation alone
edges.decisive_discriminant: Parenteral anticoagulation treats thrombin generation but does not replace the recommended aspirin loading dose when there is no absolute aspirin contraindication.
excluded_contexts: Exclude true aspirin anaphylaxis or another absolute aspirin contraindication; an alternative antiplatelet pathway then requires separate evidence.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select urgent transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis when diagnostic STEMI has an absolute fibrinolysis contraindication, even though expected device time exceeds the usual pharmacoinvasive threshold.
edges.plausible_error: The learner follows the delay threshold but fails to apply the absolute-contraindication override.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis despite the absolute contraindication
edges.decisive_discriminant: Any prior intracranial hemorrhage is an absolute fibrinolysis contraindication; the delay-based pharmacoinvasive branch is therefore prohibited and urgent PPCI transfer is required.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a remote ischemic stroke without hemorrhage; timing and contraindication classification would differ.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select urgent transfer for primary PCI without fibrinolysis when diagnostic STEMI has an absolute fibrinolysis contraindication, even though expected device time exceeds the usual pharmacoinvasive threshold.
edges.plausible_error: The learner mistakes a contraindication to one reperfusion method for a contraindication to all reperfusion.
edges.neighboring_choice: Provide medical therapy without an urgent reperfusion pathway
edges.decisive_discriminant: The fibrinolysis contraindication redirects rather than cancels reperfusion; CCS/CAIC guidance calls for PPCI transfer even when device time will exceed 120 minutes.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a late asymptomatic presentation for which routine reperfusion may no longer be indicated.

applicable_learner_decisions: Recognize post-MI papillary muscle rupture causing acute severe mitral regurgitation from the timing, abrupt pulmonary edema, hypotension, and new apical systolic murmur.
edges.plausible_error: The learner recognizes a mechanical complication but does not localize the structural lesion.
edges.neighboring_choice: Post-MI ventricular septal rupture
edges.decisive_discriminant: Papillary rupture produces acute severe often eccentric MR with pulmonary edema and possible mobile LV tissue; VSR is defined by septal discontinuity and a left-to-right shunt on Doppler.
excluded_contexts: Exclude echocardiographic evidence of a left-to-right septal shunt.

applicable_learner_decisions: Recognize post-MI papillary muscle rupture causing acute severe mitral regurgitation from the timing, abrupt pulmonary edema, hypotension, and new apical systolic murmur.
edges.plausible_error: The learner attributes any post-MI collapse to free-wall rupture without using the pulmonary and echocardiographic pattern.
edges.neighboring_choice: Post-MI free-wall rupture with tamponade
edges.decisive_discriminant: Free-wall rupture is distinguished by pericardial effusion or tamponade and possible electromechanical dissociation; papillary rupture instead produces acute severe MR with abrupt pulmonary edema.
excluded_contexts: Exclude pericardial effusion, tamponade physiology, or electromechanical dissociation.

applicable_learner_decisions: Recognize post-MI papillary muscle rupture causing acute severe mitral regurgitation from the timing, abrupt pulmonary edema, hypotension, and new apical systolic murmur.
shared_features: chest symptoms and biomarker abnormalities may recur
edges.plausible_error: The learner labels all post-MI deterioration as recurrent ischemia and ignores the new murmur and acute-MR physiology.
edges.neighboring_choice: Recurrent ischemia without a mechanical complication
edges.decisive_discriminant: Recurrent ischemia is supported by recurrent ischemic pain with recurrent ST elevation and biomarker re-elevation; a new apical systolic murmur, abrupt pulmonary edema, and severe MR on echo identify papillary muscle rupture.
excluded_contexts: Exclude recurrent ischemic ECG/biomarker changes without a new structural echocardiographic lesion.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select an emergent cardiothoracic surgical repair pathway after echocardiography confirms post-MI ventricular septal rupture with hemodynamic collapse.
shared_features: vasoactive and mechanical support may improve perfusion
edges.plausible_error: The learner mistakes bridge stabilization for definitive closure of the defect.
edges.neighboring_choice: Continue medical stabilization without urgent surgical referral
edges.decisive_discriminant: Medical or short-term mechanical support is a bridge; confirmed VSR with collapse requires immediate surgical-centre management and urgent definitive-closure planning.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a goals-of-care decision for palliation after multidisciplinary discussion.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select an emergent cardiothoracic surgical repair pathway after echocardiography confirms post-MI ventricular septal rupture with hemodynamic collapse.
shared_features: coronary occlusion caused the index infarct
angiography may be part of the operative work-up
edges.plausible_error: The learner assumes reopening the culprit artery will close an established septal rupture.
edges.neighboring_choice: Perform coronary PCI as the only definitive intervention
edges.decisive_discriminant: PCI can treat coronary disease but cannot close the established left-to-right septal defect; definitive surgical or selected structural closure is required.
excluded_contexts: Exclude an index MI without a confirmed mechanical septal defect.

applicable_learner_decisions: Select an emergent cardiothoracic surgical repair pathway after echocardiography confirms post-MI ventricular septal rupture with hemodynamic collapse.
shared_features: delayed repair can be considered after monitored stabilization
fresh infarct tissue is surgically fragile
edges.plausible_error: The learner converts an individualized in-hospital bridge-to-repair strategy into unsafe outpatient delay despite collapse.
edges.neighboring_choice: Plan elective repair after discharge despite hemodynamic collapse
edges.decisive_discriminant: Although exact operative timing is individualized, collapse mandates urgent surgical-centre care and continuous bridge-to-definitive-repair planning; discharge for elective repair is not an acceptable pathway.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a hemodynamically stable patient already under continuous inpatient Heart Team surveillance for a planned delayed repair.

applicable_learner_decisions: Admit high-risk NSTE-ACS for early invasive coronary evaluation rather than discharge or outpatient testing when dynamic ischemic ECG changes and a troponin rise are present despite symptom resolution.
shared_features: current vital signs may be stable
edges.plausible_error: The learner overweights one reassuring observation and ignores objective high-risk ECG and troponin findings.
edges.neighboring_choice: Discharge after one reassuring observation despite objective high-risk features
edges.decisive_discriminant: Dynamic ischemic ST/T change plus an acute troponin rise meets high-risk NSTE-ACS criteria and requires admission for early invasive evaluation, irrespective of current pain resolution.
excluded_contexts: Exclude a validated low-risk rule-out pathway with serial negative biomarkers and no ischemic ECG change.

applicable_learner_decisions: Admit high-risk NSTE-ACS for early invasive coronary evaluation rather than discharge or outpatient testing when dynamic ischemic ECG changes and a troponin rise are present despite symptom resolution.
shared_features: noninvasive stress testing can risk-stratify lower-risk chest pain
the patient is currently symptom free
edges.plausible_error: The learner applies a lower-risk chest-pain disposition to confirmed high-risk NSTE-ACS.
edges.neighboring_choice: Arrange outpatient stress testing
edges.decisive_discriminant: Outpatient stress testing belongs to a lower-risk or uncertain pathway; objective dynamic ischemia and troponin rise require inpatient early invasive coronary evaluation.
excluded_contexts: Exclude lower-risk NSTE-ACS or possible ACS with normal serial biomarkers and no dynamic ischemic ECG changes.

applicable_learner_decisions: Admit high-risk NSTE-ACS for early invasive coronary evaluation rather than discharge or outpatient testing when dynamic ischemic ECG changes and a troponin rise are present despite symptom resolution.
edges.plausible_error: The learner delays committing to the invasive pathway despite established high-risk criteria.
edges.neighboring_choice: Continue observation without an invasive evaluation plan
edges.decisive_discriminant: Observation alone does not satisfy the recommended early invasive strategy for high-risk NSTE-ACS; dynamic ST/T changes and troponin rise determine the inpatient invasive plan.
excluded_contexts: Exclude brief monitored stabilization while transfer or early angiography is actively being arranged.
